question: Mehrangarh Fort is located in which of the following cities?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jodhpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mehrangarh**, a historic fort situated in** Jodhpur, Rajasthan**, India, commands a prominent position atop a hill, soaring approximately 122 meters above the surrounding plains.
 
• Covering an expansive area of 1,200 acres (486 hectares), the fort was initially constructed circa 1459 by Rao Jodha, the Rajput ruler of the Rathore clan. However, the majority of the existing structure dates back to the 17th century.
 
• Featuring seven gates, including the primary entrance known as Jai Pol, signifying 'victory gate,' erected by Maharaja Man Singh to commemorate his triumphs over the Jaipur and Bikaner armies in 1806.
 
• Another notable gate is the Fattehpol, translating to 'victory gate,' symbolizing Maharaja Ajit Singh's victory over the Mughals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jodhpur, **the second-largest city in the Indian state of Rajasthan, holds the official status of being the state's second metropolitan city.
 
• Serving as the administrative hub for both the Jodhpur district and Jodhpur division, the city boasts a rich historical legacy as the former capital of the Kingdom of Marwar, now integrated into Rajasthan.
 
• Renowned as a sought-after tourist destination, Jodhpur enchants visitors with its array of palaces, forts, and temples, nestled amidst the rugged terrain of the Thar Desert.
 
• It earns its moniker "Blue City" due to the distinctive light blue hue adorning the buildings in its oldest district.
